annotations.description: Missed a land drop on turn 3 with Transguild Promenade in hand. With a hand full of expensive spells (Wild Ricochet at 4 mana, Jaya's Immolating Inferno needing X+RR), getting to 4 lands next turn is important. They had 3 untapped lands to pay the {1} ETB cost, and nothing productive to do with the remaining 2 mana this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without playing any land, missing the turn 3 land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Transguild Promenade, pay {1} to keep it, then pass. This gets to 4 lands on turn 4 and advances toward casting the expensive spells in hand.

annotations.description: GLM47 Heckler cast Timely Ward before playing their land (Transguild Promenade) for the turn. While both could be done this turn (play Transguild Promenade paying {1}, then cast Timely Ward for {2}{W} with remaining lands), casting the spell first means if something goes wrong or priorities change, the land drop is wasted. Standard practice is to play lands before casting spells to maximize information and flexibility.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Timely Ward on Wyleth before playing Transguild Promenade from hand
annotations.betterLine: Play Transguild Promenade first (paying {1}), then cast Timely Ward on Wyleth with remaining mana

annotations.description: Fetching 2 Plains when the hand is heavily blue-leaning (Behold the Multiverse, Mulldrifter, Surtland Elementalist needing UU, Windfall all need blue). With only Island and Azorius Guildgate as current blue sources, adding no Islands makes it very difficult to cast Surtland Elementalist (UU) and creates unnecessary color problems.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected 2 Plains from library with Burnished Hart
annotations.betterLine: Fetch 1 Island + 1 Plains (or 2 Islands) to better support the blue-heavy hand, especially Surtland Elementalist's UU requirement. With Sejiri Refuge and Azorius Guildgate already providing white, one Plains is sufficient for Sun Titan's WW.

annotations.description: Should play a land before spending mana on leveling up Echo Mage. Playing Temple of the False God first would give 8 mana total (Temple produces 2 with 5+ lands), allowing both Mirari (5 mana) and a level up on Echo Mage (2 mana) in the same turn, rather than just a level up.
annotations.actionTaken: Leveled up Echo Mage for {1}{U} before playing a land
annotations.betterLine: Play Temple of the False God first (giving 8 mana total), then potentially cast Mirari (5) and level up Echo Mage (2) in the same turn, getting significantly more value from the turn.

annotations.description: Fetched Mountain when already having 3 Mountains and only 1 Plains, with two white spells in hand (Dawn Charm, Condemn). Plains would better balance the mana base for the white-heavy hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Mountain from Evolving Wilds, going to 4 Mountains and 1 Plains
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Plains to go to 2 Plains and 3 Mountains, better supporting the two white spells in hand and providing more color flexibility

annotations.description: Burnished Hart would have been significantly better here. Sun Titan is already on the battlefield without haste, so Swiftfoot Boots doesn't enable an immediate attack - Sun Titan can't attack this turn regardless since it was just cast in postcombat main. Burnished Hart comes back to the battlefield and can be sacrificed for 3 mana to fetch two basic lands, providing substantial ramp. With 7 lands, getting to 9 lands would help cast expensive cards like Surtland Elementalist (7 mana). Swiftfoot Boots only costs 1 to equip, but the hexproof/haste is less impactful than ramping by 2 lands when you have expensive cards in hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Returned Swiftfoot Boots from graveyard to battlefield with Sun Titan's ETB trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Return Burnished Hart from graveyard to battlefield, then sacrifice it next turn (or later) to fetch two basic lands, enabling casting Surtland Elementalist and other expensive spells sooner.

annotations.description: GLM47 Heckler targeted themselves with Jaya's Immolating Inferno, dealing 3 damage to their own face for no reason. The spell deals X damage to up to three targets, and they chose themselves as one of the three targets alongside two opponents. There is absolutely no benefit to dealing 3 damage to yourself.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Haiku Stoic, Sonnet Timmy, and themselves (GLM47 Heckler) with Jaya's Immolating Inferno for X=3, dealing 3 damage to each.
annotations.betterLine: Target the three opponents (Haiku Stoic, Sonnet Timmy, and Grok4F Libby) to deal 3 damage to each of them, or target two opponents and Echo Mage to remove a threatening creature.

annotations.description: With 5 white sources and only 3 blue sources, and a hand containing Surtland Elementalist (5UU), Mulldrifter (4U), Behold the Multiverse (3U), and Windfall (2U), fetching a Plains is wasteful. The mana base is already white-heavy and the hand is entirely blue-demanding. Plus there's a Plains in hand to play next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Planned to fetch Plains + Island for 'balance'
annotations.betterLine: Fetch two Islands to fix the blue-heavy hand, especially to enable Surtland Elementalist's UU requirement. Already have 5 white sources plus a Plains in hand.

annotations.description: Player misunderstood Rousing Refrain's effect entirely, thinking it deals damage rather than generating red mana equal to the target opponent's hand size. The optimal target should be whichever opponent has the most cards in hand to maximize mana generation. Sonnet Timmy, having deployed a 6-mana Sun Titan, likely has fewer cards in hand than other opponents.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Sonnet Timmy with Rousing Refrain based on incorrect belief that the card deals damage
annotations.betterLine: Should have targeted the opponent with the most cards in hand (likely GLM47 Heckler who has deployed only lands and may be holding more cards) to maximize the red mana generated for follow-up plays

annotations.description: Sonnet Timmy cast Warhorn Blast for its full cost of 4W (5 mana) to pump only a single creature (Sun Titan) by +2/+1, making it an 8/7 instead of 6/6 for one attack. This is very poor value - spending 5 mana and a card for +2 damage. Foretelling it for 2 mana now and casting it later for 2W would save 2 mana total, and more importantly, the card could be saved for a turn when there are multiple creatures to buff. With only Sun Titan on the board, the +2/+1 buff is minimal impact for a full card. Additionally, casting it at full cost leaves Sonnet Timmy with less mana available, when foretelling would preserve the card for a more impactful future turn while only costing 2 mana now.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Warhorn Blast at full cost (4W) during combat to give Sun Titan +2/+1, spending 5 mana and a card for just 2 extra damage.
annotations.betterLine: Foretell Warhorn Blast for 2 mana (or even 0 mana if done earlier), saving it for a turn with multiple creatures on board for much greater impact. The 2 extra damage on Sun Titan is not worth a full card and 5 mana.

annotations.description: Fetching 2 Plains when nearly every card in hand requires blue mana (Behold the Multiverse, Surtland Elementalist needing UU, Windfall). While there's an Island in hand to play, fetching at least 1 Island would provide more reliable access to the UU needed for Surtland Elementalist and general blue mana requirements.
annotations.actionTaken: Planned to fetch 2 Plains from library
annotations.betterLine: Fetch 1 Island + 1 Plains to better support the blue-heavy hand (especially Surtland Elementalist's UU requirement), while still having ample white sources

annotations.description: Guttersnipe is a 2/2 creature that deals 2 damage to each opponent when you cast instants/sorceries, which synergizes well with Mirari already on the battlefield. However, Arcane Melee (reducing instant/sorcery costs by 2) also synergizes powerfully with Mirari and the spell-heavy deck. With 8 mana available (Island, Swamp, Izzet Guildgate, Island, Swamp, Swamp, Mirari, Mountain), casting Arcane Melee for 5 mana would leave 3 mana open (enough to potentially copy spells with Mirari next turn for cheaper). Guttersnipe costs 3 mana but is vulnerable as a 2/2 creature - it could be easily killed. Arcane Melee as an enchantment is harder to remove and provides immediate cost reduction that compounds with Mirari. That said, Guttersnipe provides damage output and the choice is defensible since the player also has Illusionist's Gambit for defense. The decision is close but Arcane Melee might have been slightly better given the Mirari synergy and greater resilience.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Guttersnipe for 3 mana
annotations.betterLine: Cast Arcane Melee for 5 mana to reduce future spell costs by 2, maximizing Mirari synergy and leaving the enchantment harder to remove than a 2/2 creature

annotations.description: Casting Arcane Melee before playing Temple of the False God from hand. Playing the land first would provide additional mana (Temple adds {C}{C} with 5+ lands) and leave mana open after casting Arcane Melee, giving more flexibility to respond to threats or hold up Illusionist's Gambit.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Arcane Melee without first playing Temple of the False God
annotations.betterLine: Play Temple of the False God first, then cast Arcane Melee, leaving 1 extra mana available and having 8 lands on board for future turns either way

annotations.description: Casting Flickerwisp during postcombat main means the exiled permanent returns at this turn's end step, making the exile nearly meaningless. If targeting Sun Titan, it actually gives the opponent a free ETB trigger to recur a permanent like Burnished Hart. Additionally, Flickerwisp would die to Heckler's own Winds of Rath in hand, making the creature investment potentially wasteful.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Flickerwisp postcombat main, providing only a temporary (same-turn) exile effect
annotations.betterLine: Hold Flickerwisp for a turn where the exile timing matters more, or play Transguild Promenade to develop mana toward casting Winds of Rath (which needs 5 mana and would answer Sun Titan). Playing the land drop first and holding up Dawn Charm/Condemn for defense would be better resource management.

annotations.description: Flickerwisp's temporary exile was used on Swiftfoot Boots, which is relatively low-impact since the equipment just returns at end step and can be re-equipped. Mirari on Grok4F Libby's board is a much more threatening permanent that enables spell copying, and denying it for a turn cycle would be more impactful.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Swiftfoot Boots with Flickerwisp's exile ETB
annotations.betterLine: Target Mirari to temporarily deny Grok4F Libby their powerful spell-copying artifact for the turn cycle, or target Sun Titan if you can remove it permanently before it returns (though that's unlikely here)

annotations.description: Cast Windfall for free instead of Behold the Multiverse, discarding Behold the Multiverse and an Island while giving all three opponents fresh hands. Behold the Multiverse for free would provide Scry 2 + draw 2 (pure card advantage) without helping opponents. Windfall symmetrically refills everyone's hands, which is especially dangerous when Grok4F Libby is at 40 life with 8 lands untapped and Sonnet Timmy only discarded 2 cards.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Windfall for free during combat, discarding Behold the Multiverse and Island, giving all players new hands
annotations.betterLine: Cast Behold the Multiverse for free to Scry 2 and draw 2 cards without giving opponents any card advantage, preserving information advantage and not refueling opponents

annotations.description: Attacking Sonnet Timmy with Guttersnipe when Sun Titan (6/6 vigilance) can block and kill the 2/2 Guttersnipe. Guttersnipe is Libby's most valuable creature due to its triggered ability dealing 2 damage to each opponent on instant/sorcery casts. While Sonnet Timmy likely won't block over 2 damage, the risk of losing Guttersnipe is unnecessary.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked Sonnet Timmy with Guttersnipe, risking it being blocked by Sun Titan (6/6).
annotations.betterLine: Attack GLM47 Heckler instead, where Flickerwisp (flying) cannot block the ground Guttersnipe, guaranteeing 2 damage with zero risk to your key creature.

annotations.description: GLM47 Heckler passed on using Word of Seizing to steal Sonnet Timmy's Sun Titan during combat. Stealing Sun Titan with split second, then attacking with it would trigger its attack ability to recur a permanent with MV ≤3 from the graveyard (e.g., Evolving Wilds, Terramorphic Expanse), while also dealing 6 damage and denying Sonnet Timmy a blocker for the turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to cast any instants during combat
annotations.betterLine: Cast Word of Seizing targeting Sun Titan to steal it, attack with both Flickerwisp and Sun Titan, using Sun Titan's attack trigger to recur a useful permanent from the graveyard

annotations.description: GLM47 Heckler is enchanting Sram, Senior Edificer with Spirit Mantle, but Sram is their own creature that appears to be a 2/2 legendary. While Sram draws a card when an Aura is cast (which triggers here), putting Spirit Mantle on Sram gives it +1/+1 and protection from creatures, making it a 3/3 unblockable attacker. However, Flickerwisp (3/1 flyer) is already a better attacker, and Sun Titan (6/6 with vigilance) belonging to Sonnet Timmy is a much bigger threat on the board. The Spirit Mantle on Flickerwisp would make a 4/2 unblockable flyer, which deals more damage per turn. On the other hand, Sram with Spirit Mantle creates a Voltron engine where future Auras and Equipment draw cards and the creature can't be blocked by creatures. This is a reasonable strategic choice for building toward a Voltron plan, especially since Sram's draw trigger already fired. The choice between Flickerwisp and Sram is debatable - Flickerwisp might get flickered or die more easily as a 3/1, while Sram as a Voltron target has long-term value with its card draw ability.
annotations.actionTaken: Enchanted Sram, Senior Edificer with Spirit Mantle
annotations.betterLine: Enchanting Flickerwisp with Spirit Mantle would create a 4/2 unblockable flyer for more immediate damage output, though Sram as a Voltron target has reasonable long-term synergy.

annotations.description: Spectral Deluge with only 1 Island on the battlefield means X=1, so it only bounces creatures with toughness 1 or less. This wastes a powerful late-game sweeper for minimal impact (only bouncing Flickerwisp). With 2 Islands still in hand, waiting to play more Islands would have made this card significantly more powerful.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Spectral Deluge with X=1, bouncing only toughness-1-or-less creatures
annotations.betterLine: Either cast Cleansing Nova (artifacts/enchantments mode to remove Arcane Melee), or hold Spectral Deluge until more Islands are in play for a much more impactful bounce effect. Playing Islands from hand first would have increased X.

annotations.description: Arcane Melee is a symmetric cost reduction that helps all players equally. Spirit Mantle on Sun Titan makes it a 7/7 with protection from creatures (unblockable in combat), which is a much more pressing threat. Propaganda also directly prevents GLM47 Heckler from attacking Grok4F Libby.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected Arcane Melee as a Return to Dust target
annotations.betterLine: Should have prioritized Spirit Mantle (making Sun Titan unblockable) or Propaganda (preventing attacks on Libby) as the higher-value exile target

annotations.description: Spirit Mantle is likely enchanting Sun Titan, making it a 7/7 with protection from creatures (unblockable, can't be blocked). This is a far more dangerous combination than Swiftfoot Boots, which only provides hexproof and haste to its equipped creature. An unblockable Sun Titan that recurs permanents every attack is one of the most threatening board states possible.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to exile Swiftfoot Boots as the second Return to Dust target
annotations.betterLine: Exile Spirit Mantle to remove protection from creatures from Sun Titan, making it blockable and vulnerable to creature-based interaction

annotations.description: Spiteful Visions deals 1 damage to each player whenever they draw a card, and gives each player an extra draw per turn. In a multiplayer game where one opponent (Haiku Stoic) is already eliminated, Grok4F Libby is at 40 life (the highest), GLM47 Heckler is at 23, and Sonnet Timmy is at 35. While Spiteful Visions does asymmetrically hurt the lower-life players more, it also gives all opponents extra cards and hurts Libby too. Sonnet Timmy has Sun Titan on board and will benefit from extra draws to find more threats. Charmbreaker Devils (5R) would be castable with 8 lands and would start recurring instants/sorceries from the graveyard while being a 4/4 threat. Decree of Pain (6BB) is not yet castable. The Spiteful Visions play is defensible as it pressures the lower-life Heckler, but giving Sonnet Timmy (who has Sun Titan and a developed board) extra cards is risky.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Spiteful Visions (4 mana) to deal damage on draws and grant extra draws to all players.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Charmbreaker Devils (6 mana, available with 8 lands including Izzet Boilerworks producing 2) to start recurring instants/sorceries from graveyard and present a threat, or cast Temple Bell + Swiftfoot Boots for more controlled card advantage.

annotations.description: Sonnet Timmy cast Cloudblazer before playing Island from hand and before attacking with Sun Titan. Playing Island first would give 8 lands, meaning after casting Cloudblazer (5 mana), they'd have 3 mana remaining - enough for Ghostly Prison. Additionally, attacking with Sun Titan first would trigger its attack ability to return a permanent with MV 3 or less from graveyard (e.g., Burnished Hart for ramp) before committing mana to Cloudblazer.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Cloudblazer without playing Island first and before combat
annotations.betterLine: Play Island, go to combat, attack with Sun Titan (returning Burnished Hart or another valuable permanent from graveyard), then cast Cloudblazer in second main phase with more mana available for additional plays

annotations.description: Dealing 2 damage to each creature when the only creature on board is Sun Titan (6/6) accomplishes virtually nothing - it survives easily. This mode is wasted.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose 'Incendiary Command deals 2 damage to each creature' as second mode, which only pings Sun Titan for 2 out of 6 toughness.
annotations.betterLine: Choose mode 3 'Destroy target nonbasic land' to destroy one of Sonnet Timmy's key nonbasic lands (like Sejiri Refuge or Azorius Guildgate), providing actual tangible value by disrupting the opponent with the biggest board threat.

annotations.description: Cast Brass Squire, a 1/3 whose only ability is attaching equipment, with no equipment on the battlefield or in hand. Meanwhile, Flickerwisp was available as a 3/1 flyer that could temporarily exile Sun Titan (the biggest threat on board) and provide meaningful board presence.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Brass Squire as a vanilla 1/3 with no equipment synergy available.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Flickerwisp to get a 3/1 flyer and temporarily exile Sun Titan or another relevant permanent. The flying body is much more relevant for both offense and defense.

annotations.description: Sonnet Timmy cast Day of the Dragons with only Sun Titan on the battlefield, exiling their powerful 6/6 vigilance creature to create just one 5/5 flying Dragon token. Sun Titan's recurring ETB/attack ability to return permanents from graveyard is extremely valuable (can recur Burnished Hart, Mulldrifter, etc.), and trading it for a single 5/5 flyer is a poor exchange. Additionally, Day of the Dragons as an enchantment is vulnerable to removal - if it's destroyed, the Dragon is sacrificed and Sun Titan returns, but the opponent could also just destroy it at an inopportune time. More importantly, Sonnet Timmy should have considered playing their land (Island or Plains) first before casting spells, and could have used Momentary Blink or Eerie Interlude on Sun Titan to get another ETB trigger to recur something from the graveyard first, THEN cast Day of the Dragons to exile and convert creatures (including any creatures returned by Sun Titan). Alternatively, Cleansing Nova could clear GLM47 Heckler's remaining board or destroy artifacts/enchantments.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Day of the Dragons with only Sun Titan on the battlefield, converting one powerful creature into one 5/5 Dragon token.
annotations.betterLine: Play a land first (Island or Plains), then use Momentary Blink on Sun Titan to get another ETB trigger (recurring Burnished Hart or Mulldrifter from graveyard), building up more creatures before eventually casting Day of the Dragons for more Dragon tokens. Or simply attack with Sun Titan to recur a permanent and hold Day of the Dragons for a turn with more creatures.

annotations.description: Sonnet Timmy passed without activating Cryptic Caves to draw a card. With 5+ lands controlled and no immediate need for the colorless mana, sacrificing Cryptic Caves for a card draw would have been pure value. Additionally, they should have played a land (Island or Plains from hand) if they hadn't already this turn to maintain land development. The reasoning about 'DRAGONS ready' doesn't match the board state where they have no creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without doing anything in postcombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: At minimum, activate Cryptic Caves to draw a card (pay {1}, tap, sacrifice). Also play a land from hand if the land drop wasn't used this turn.

annotations.description: Cast Mask of Avacyn before playing a land drop. They have several lands in hand (Slayers' Stronghold, Stone Quarry, Forgotten Cave, Rupture Spire) and should play a land first before casting spells. Slayers' Stronghold in particular provides excellent utility with its haste/vigilance activation. Additionally, casting Mask with no creatures on board is low-impact when Flickerwisp could be cast first to provide a body.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Mask of Avacyn ({2}) with no creatures on the battlefield, before making a land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Slayers' Stronghold first (free land drop providing haste utility), then cast Flickerwisp ({1}{W}{W} = 3 mana) to get a creature on board, then cast Mask of Avacyn ({2} = 2 mana), then equip ({3} = 3 mana) using all 9 available mana for a hexproof 4/3 flyer.

annotations.description: Declined to activate Evolving Wilds, which is a free activation that thins the deck and provides an additional land. There's no downside to cracking Evolving Wilds at any point since it's pure upside.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate any abilities while Tempt with Reflections was on the stack
annotations.betterLine: Activate Evolving Wilds to search for a basic land, thinning the deck for free value

annotations.description: Declined to crack Evolving Wilds during upkeep. With Dimir Guildgate in hand as a land drop, sacrificing Evolving Wilds would net an additional land on battlefield (searching for a basic), ramping from 8 to potentially 10 lands this turn. This is pure upside mana development.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate Evolving Wilds (chose False)
annotations.betterLine: Activate Evolving Wilds to search for a basic land (likely Swamp or Island), putting it onto the battlefield tapped, then play Dimir Guildgate as the land drop for the turn to maximize mana development.

annotations.description: Sonnet Timmy has no creatures on the battlefield but believed they had four 5/5 dragons. They skipped their entire precombat main phase without playing a land (Island in hand) or casting any spells. They had mana available for Sea Gate Oracle (2U) to get a body and card selection, and could have played Island first for additional mana. Against the only remaining opponent at 34 life, developing the board is critical.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the entire precombat main phase without playing a land or casting any spells, then skipped attack with no creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island, then cast Sea Gate Oracle (for card selection and a body), potentially followed by other plays. At minimum, don't skip the land drop.

annotations.description: Sea Gate Oracle is on the stack, and Sonnet Timmy has Restoration Angel in hand which could flash in to flicker the Sea Gate Oracle when it enters the battlefield, drawing an extra card (getting two Sea Gate Oracle triggers instead of one). This is a clear value opportunity being missed. Additionally, Momentary Blink could serve the same purpose after the Oracle resolves. The player declined all options citing being 'stuck in a loop' rather than recognizing the value play.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority while Sea Gate Oracle was on the stack, declining to use Restoration Angel or plan for a flicker.
annotations.betterLine: Let Sea Gate Oracle resolve, then cast Restoration Angel targeting Sea Gate Oracle to get a second enters-the-battlefield trigger, netting an extra card selection. Alternatively, after Oracle resolves, cast Momentary Blink on it for the same effect at lower mana cost.

annotations.description: Casting Soulherder with no creatures on the battlefield means it's just a 1/1 body with no immediate blink value. Restoration Angel is a much better standalone creature as a 3/4 flyer that applies real pressure in a 1v1 against an opponent at 34 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Soulherder (a 1/1 with no creatures to blink)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Restoration Angel (3/4 flyer) as the first creature to establish board presence and start applying meaningful pressure. Soulherder could be deployed later alongside creatures to blink for value.

annotations.betterLine: Activate Cryptic Caves (pay {1} with untapped Plains, tap and sacrifice Cryptic Caves) to draw a card, converting an otherwise unused colorless land into card advantage.

annotations.betterLine: Activate Evolving Wilds to search for a basic land, getting free deck thinning and ensuring the land untaps by next turn.

annotations.betterLine: Activate Evolving Wilds to search for a basic land, thinning the deck and improving future draws. Temple Bell activation is more debatable but could also be correct to pressure Sonnet Timmy's life total via Spiteful Visions.

annotations.betterLine: Exile both Propaganda and Ghostly Prison to fully remove the attack tax, enabling free attacks against Grok4F Libby and pursuing a faster kill plan.
